```{python}
#| tags: [setup]
import sys, os
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath("."))
from _pcpkg import *  # noqa: F401,F403
import doe_report as D
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import scipy.stats as sstat

DOC = "PCP-003"
UO = "bioreactor"
UO_TITLE = "Production Bioreactor (Step 3)"

# --- doc-local derived scalars (pulled from the model; never typed) ---------------
STEP = CFG.unit_op(UO).step
SCALE_L = f"{CFG.meta['commercial_scale_l']:,}"
N_MC = f"{V['n_monte_carlo']:,}"
N_PAR_MC = f"{D.PAR_MC_N:,}"

# Study scope, from the parameter register.
_pp = plan_params(UO)
n_par = len(_pp)
n_par_mv = int((_pp["Study type"] == "multivariate").sum())
n_par_uni = int((_pp["Study type"] == "univariate").sum())
_cq = cqas_for(UO)
n_cqa = len(_cq)
n_cqa_noncrit = int((~_cq["Criticality"].isin(("H", "VH"))).sum())
n_glyc = int((_cq["Category"] == "glycosylation").sum())
n_resp = len(D.responses(UO))

# Design structure, read from the seeded designs rather than assumed.
scr_f, rsm_f = D.screening_factors(UO), D.rsm_factors(UO)
k_scr, k_rsm = len(scr_f), len(rsm_f)
n_scr, n_rsm = doe_runs(UO, "screening"), doe_runs(UO, "rsm")
n_scr_c, n_rsm_c = doe_centre_points(UO, "screening"), doe_centre_points(UO, "rsm")
_rsm_csv = csv(f"doe_{UO}_rsm.csv")
n_scr_fact = int((csv(f"doe_{UO}_screening.csv").run_type == "factorial").sum())
n_rsm_fact = int((_rsm_csv.run_type == "factorial").sum())
n_rsm_ax = int((_rsm_csv.run_type == "axial").sum())
n_full = 2 ** k_scr

# Model sizes and the degrees of freedom they leave.
n_2fi = k_scr * (k_scr - 1) // 2
n_scr_terms = 1 + k_scr + n_2fi
df_scr = n_scr - n_scr_terms
df_pe_scr = n_scr_c - 1
n_rsm_terms = 1 + 2 * k_rsm + k_rsm * (k_rsm - 1) // 2
n_rsm_quad = k_rsm
df_rsm = n_rsm - n_rsm_terms
df_pe_rsm = n_rsm_c - 1

# Formatting closures over this step's parameter register (values stay in config).
def _p(f):
    return CFG.unit_op(UO).param(f)

def sp_of(f, unit=True):
    p = _p(f)
    return f"{p.setpoint:g} {p.unit}" if unit else f"{p.setpoint:g}"

def nor_of(f, unit=True):
    p = _p(f)
    s = f"{p.nor[0]:g}–{p.nor[1]:g}"
    return f"{s} {p.unit}" if unit else s

def rng_of(f, unit=True):
    p = _p(f)
    s = f"{p.prange[0]:g}–{p.prange[1]:g}"
    return f"{s} {p.unit}" if unit else s
```

# Purpose and scope {#sec-purpose}

This plan describes the process characterization studies that will be performed on the
A-Mab production bioreactor before the drug substance process is qualified at the receiving
site (`{python} RECEIVING_SITE`). The bioreactor is Step `{python} STEP` of the drug
substance process and is operated as a fed-batch cell culture at `{python} SCALE_L` L. It is
the step at which the glycosylation, charge variant and aggregate attributes of A-Mab are
formed, and because the glycan attributes in particular are not modified by the platform
purification train, the design space established here carries most of the product quality
argument for the upstream process.

The studies will be executed on a qualified scale-down model at the sending site
(`{python} SENDING_SITE`). Their results, the design space that follows from them and the
classification of every parameter will be reported in the paired report (PCR-003). Nothing
in this plan states an outcome. It states what will be run, how the data will be analysed,
and the criteria against which the analysis will be judged.

The work follows the enhanced, quality by design development approach, and it forms part of
the Stage 1 process design record for the drug substance [@fda2011; @ichq8; @ichq11]. The
scope of the study was set by the pre-characterization risk assessment (RA-001), and the
campaign-level framework it sits inside, which covers the common scale-down approach, the
common statistical approach and the acceptance framework, is given in the master plan
(PCMP-001).

The plan covers the `{python} n_par` process parameters of the production bioreactor listed
in @tbl-params, of which `{python} n_par_mv` will be studied in a multivariate design and
`{python} n_par_uni` will be assessed one at a time, in accordance with the study assignment
made in RA-001 and not re-derived here. It also covers the `{python} n_cqa` quality
attributes that the drug substance register assigns to this step (@tbl-cqa), of which
`{python} n_resp` are measured as design responses.

Four things are outside the scope of this plan. Vial thaw, seed expansion and the N-1 seed
bioreactor are not characterized, because prior knowledge and the risk assessment place no
product quality risk on them (@sec-risk). Harvest and clarification are covered by the
harvest plan (PCP-004). The clearance of host cell protein (HCP) and residual DNA by the
purification train is covered by PCP-005, PCP-007 and PCP-008. Confirmation of the design
space at commercial scale belongs to Stage 2, and it follows the process performance
qualification strategy set out in the transfer plan (PTP-001).

# Objectives {#sec-objectives}

The study has five objectives, and each one produces a defined section of PCR-003.

1. Quantify the relationship between the multivariate process parameters and the quality
   attributes this step forms, over ranges wider than the normal operating ranges (NORs).
2. Define the design space for the well-controlled culture parameters, which is the
   multivariate region within which every attribute in @tbl-cqa is predicted to meet its
   acceptance criterion.
3. Establish a proven acceptable range (PAR) for each parameter against each attribute it
   governs, and confirm that the normal operating range sits inside it.
4. Provide the demonstrated effects and the control capability needed to classify each
   parameter under the classification procedure (SOP-4001).
5. Justify the parameter ranges that will be carried into Stage 2, and state this step's
   contribution to the control strategy for the drug substance.

The first two objectives depend on a design of experiments, the third on the fitted
response-surface model, and the last two on both of those together with prior knowledge. If
the scale-down model fails its qualification (@sec-sdm), none of the five can be met, which
is why qualification is the first activity in the sequence given in @sec-schedule.

# Prior knowledge and quality risk basis {#sec-prior}

Prior knowledge and RA-001 together fix the scope of this study. The platform is
established, so the studies described below confirm and bound known behaviour instead of
discovering it. What prior knowledge does not establish is how the culture parameters
interact over ranges wider than routine control.

## Unit-operation description and prior knowledge {#sec-uo}

The production bioreactor is a fed-batch cell culture in a stirred tank, operated with
controlled pH, temperature, dissolved oxygen (DO) and nutrient feeding, and harvested at a
fixed culture age. A-Mab is a humanized IgG1 antibody whose primary mechanism of action is
antibody-dependent cell-mediated cytotoxicity (ADCC), so the glycan attributes formed in the
culture are linked to efficacy [@amab2009]. The glycosylation and charge variant
distributions are established inside the cell and in the culture fluid, and neither is
substantially modified by the platform purification train, which means that the values
delivered at harvest are close to the values that reach drug substance.

Novacyte has operated this platform for three earlier humanized IgG1 antibodies (X-Mab,
Y-Mab and Z-Mab) and through the A-Mab clinical and engineering campaigns. That experience
establishes the mechanisms this study expects to see, and it is the reason the study can be
designed around `{python} n_par_mv` parameters instead of the full parameter list. The
expectations are set out below so that the results reported in PCR-003 either confirm them
or contradict them.

Culture pH acts on the intracellular and Golgi pH, and therefore on the activity of the
glycosyltransferases and glycosidases that finish the glycan. It also shifts lactate
metabolism and the integral of viable cell concentration, so it is expected to move several
responses at once. Culture temperature governs growth rate and specific productivity, and a
lower temperature slows growth, extends the production phase and raises the integral of
viable cell concentration, which is the route by which it reaches the glycan profile.
Dissolved carbon dioxide accumulates with scale and with the sparging strategy, and elevated
pCO~2~ lowers intracellular pH and reduces both the integral of viable cell concentration
and the titre [@amab2009]. Osmolality rises through feeding and base addition, and is
expected to act on specific productivity and on glycan processing.

Culture duration is expected to carry the largest effect on afucosylation and
galactosylation, and on the impurity load delivered to harvest. A longer culture means that a
larger fraction of the product is made by an ageing, less viable population, with released
glycosidases in the fluid and reduced nucleotide sugar availability inside the cell, so both
the glycan profile and the aggregate burden are expected to move with harvest day. The same
ageing raises the host cell protein and DNA load delivered to harvest [@amab2009]. High
mannose behaves differently from the other two glycan attributes,
because it reflects incomplete processing of the precursor and not the addition of a
terminal residue, and it is therefore expected to respond to whatever changes the residence
time of the glycoprotein in the Golgi (principally culture pH).

This step does not act alone on every attribute in its register. Aggregate formed here is
polished principally at cation exchange (PCP-007), the host cell protein and DNA burden is
cleared at Protein A, cation exchange and anion exchange (PCP-005, PCP-007 and PCP-008), and
the low-pH hold contributes a small aggregate increase of its own (PCP-006). The bioreactor
sets the input to that train, and the acceptance argument for the two process impurities is
completed downstream, not here.

## Quality attributes in scope {#sec-cqas}

@tbl-cqa lists the quality attributes that the drug substance register assigns to this step,
with the acceptance criterion and the criticality of each.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(cqas_for(UO))
print()
print(": Quality attributes formed at the production bioreactor, with acceptance criteria "
      "and criticality. Tool #1 is the product of impact and uncertainty from the "
      "attribute assessment [@amab2009]. {#tbl-cqa}")
```

Criticality is treated as a continuum and not as a binary split [@ichq9]. Attributes at the
high and very high levels are called critical, and they are the ones that drive the design
of this study. High mannose is the only attribute at the very high level, and it carries the
highest Tool #1 score in the table, because a high impact score is compounded by genuine
uncertainty about the level at which the attribute affects clearance. Afucosylation and
galactosylation sit at the high level and are linked to potency through ADCC and
complement-dependent cytotoxicity (CDC) respectively. Aggregates are also at the high level,
and their acceptance limit is taken from prior X-Mab clinical experience.

The table also lists `{python} n_cqa_noncrit` attributes that are in scope for a reason other
than their criticality. Acidic charge variants (deamidation) score at the very low level, but
the bioreactor establishes the baseline charge variant distribution and the downstream steps
change it only slightly, so the response is retained in the design and modelled with the
others. Host cell protein and residual DNA are generated by the culture and are therefore
assigned to this step, but neither is a design response of this study, because their
acceptance is achieved by clearance in the purification train and their burden at harvest is
characterized under PCP-004 and PCP-005.

All `{python} n_resp` responses are modelled here, because the culture sets the level of each
one. The `{python} n_glyc` glycan responses (afucosylation, galactosylation and high mannose)
are not modified by the purification train, so their values at harvest are the values that
reach drug substance. Acidic variants are changed only slightly downstream, and aggregate is
polished principally at cation exchange (PCP-007), so for those two responses this step sets
the input to the purification train and not the final level.

## Risk-based prioritization of parameters {#sec-risk}

RA-001 assigned each parameter of this step to a study type by risk ranking and filtering,
and this plan executes that assignment. Each parameter was ranked twice, once on its
potential impact on a quality attribute (the main effect) and once on its potential to
interact with other parameters, and the two rankings were combined into a study decision
[@amab2009]. Where no data or rationale existed to support an assessment, the parameter was
ranked at the highest level.

The outcome is `{python} n_par_mv` parameters carried into the multivariate design and
`{python} n_par_uni` assessed one at a time. Culture pH, culture temperature, dissolved
carbon dioxide, osmolality and culture duration all act on the glycan and charge variant
chemistry through the mechanisms given in @sec-uo, and all `{python} k_scr` are expected to
interact, which is what places them in a single factorial design instead of a series of
one-factor studies. Dissolved oxygen and initial viable cell concentration (iVCC) act
through growth and the integral of viable cell concentration and not through the glycan
processing chemistry itself, so a one-at-a-time assessment bounds them adequately. Basal
medium concentration and nutrient feed-1 volume are set by recipe and delivered by weight,
and platform studies have found the effect of medium concentration on afucosylation to be
statistically detectable but shallow across the full range [@amab2009]. Nutrient feed-1
volume acts through the same nutrient availability and is expected to behave in the same way.

The characterization ranges in @tbl-params are deliberately wider than the normal operating
ranges, and the expansion serves three purposes. It bounds the knowledge space, so that the
severity of a parameter excursion can later be judged against data instead of against
judgement. It supports movement within the design space once the process is licensed, which
is the practical value of a wide characterized region. It also gives the response-surface
model enough leverage to resolve curvature, which a design run only over the routine control
range cannot do, because the signal there is small against the analytical noise. The width of
each range follows from the mechanism given in @sec-uo and from the normal operating range it
surrounds, and every parameter is studied beyond that range at both edges (@tbl-params).
Platform experience bounds the upper edges in particular. A culture held at high pH and high
temperature to a late harvest loses viability quickly at the end of the run, and that
condition delivers the highest host cell protein and DNA burden to harvest [@amab2009].

# Materials and methods {#sec-methods}

## Scale-down model and its qualification {#sec-sdm}

Every study in this plan will be run on a bench-scale stirred tank bioreactor system that
has been qualified as a model of the commercial vessel under SOP-1001. The conclusions of
the study are applied directly to the commercial process, so qualification of the model is
essential and is not a formality [@fda2011].

The bench-scale and commercial vessels are stirred tanks with equivalent design
characteristics (mixing, aeration and mass transfer) and equivalent process control
capability (pH, dissolved oxygen, temperature and nutrient addition). For the qualification
runs the scale-independent parameters are operated at the commercial target values, and
these include pH, temperature, initial viable cell concentration, dissolved oxygen and
culture duration. The scale-dependent parameters are treated differently. Agitation, gas
flow rates, pressure, working volume and the resulting pCO~2~ are established at small scale
so that process performance matches the full-scale vessel [@amab2009].

Qualification will compare replicate bench-scale runs at the target condition against the
at-scale data set from the A-Mab engineering and clinical campaigns. The comparison covers
the growth and productivity profile (peak viable cell density, viability at harvest and
titre) and the `{python} n_resp` product quality responses. Each compared attribute is judged
by an equivalence assessment against a pre-defined acceptance margin, so that a difference
between scales is separated from run to run variability. The margins and the comparison
itself are defined in the qualification protocol issued under SOP-1001 and are not restated
here. Qualification will be complete and approved before any characterization run is executed.

The centre-point runs built into both designs serve a second purpose beyond the design
itself. Their replicate spread is the pure error estimate against which lack of fit is
tested (@sec-stats), and it is also a running check that the scale-down model has not
drifted between the screening campaign and the response-surface campaign.

## Cell line, media and culture operation {#sec-operation}

The culture will be inoculated from the A-Mab working cell bank and expanded through the
platform seed train to the inoculation density given in @tbl-params. Basal medium and feeds
are chemically defined and are prepared under SOP-2004. The production culture is operated
fed-batch under SOP-2003, with feed additions on a fixed schedule expressed as a percentage
of working volume, pH controlled by carbon dioxide sparging and base addition, and dissolved
oxygen controlled by the gas mix. The remaining multivariate factors are set indirectly.
Dissolved carbon dioxide is imposed by the composition and flow of the sparge and overlay gas,
and osmolality by the feed and base addition strategy. Both are verified against the daily
metabolite panel described in @sec-sampling.

Raw materials and inputs that are controlled to platform specification are not
characterization factors. Medium and feed lots, gas supply, base solution and the working
cell bank are identity and quality controlled on receipt and on use, and their control
belongs to the routine control strategy and not to this study. Any lot change during
execution will be recorded against the affected runs.

## Analytical methods {#sec-analytics}

@tbl-amv lists the validated methods that will generate the study data. Method performance,
including accuracy, precision, specificity and range, is reported in the corresponding
validation report and is not reproduced in PCR-003.

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(sop_table(sops=[], amvs=AMV_REFS))
print()
print(": Validated analytical methods supporting the study responses. {#tbl-amv}")
```

Released N-glycan mapping by 2-AB HILIC-UPLC (SOP-3010, validated under AMV-3010) reports
afucosylation, galactosylation and high mannose from a single separation, so those
`{python} n_glyc` responses share an assay and share its variance. Aggregates are measured by SEC-HPLC
(SOP-3011, AMV-3011) and reported as the high molecular weight percentage. Acidic charge
variants are measured by icIEF (SOP-3013, AMV-3013). Host cell protein by ELISA (SOP-3012,
AMV-3012) and residual DNA by qPCR (SOP-3014, AMV-3014) will be run on the harvested culture
fluid to document the burden delivered to the purification train, and, as stated in
@sec-cqas, neither is a design response here.

Assay variance matters to the interpretation of small effects. Where an estimated effect is
of the same order as the reproducibility of its assay, PCR-003 will say so, and will
attribute the variation to the method and not to the parameter. The centre-point replicate
spread reported in PCR-003 is the basis for that judgement, and the method validation reports
listed in @tbl-amv give the independent estimate against which it is checked.

## Sampling plan {#sec-sampling}

Each run will be sampled daily for viable cell density, viability and the routine metabolite
panel (glucose, lactate, ammonium, osmolality and pCO~2~), which supports the process
performance narrative and confirms that each run held the factor settings it was assigned.
The product quality panel is taken at harvest from clarified culture fluid, so that every
response is measured on material in the same state and the comparison across runs is not
confounded by the clarification step.

Both designs carry replicated centre points at the set-point condition. The screening design
has `{python} n_scr_c` centre-point runs and the response-surface design has
`{python} n_rsm_c`, which give `{python} df_pe_scr` and `{python} df_pe_rsm` degrees of
freedom for pure error respectively. Run order will be randomized within each campaign under
SOP-1002, so that any drift in the analytical methods or in the seed expansion is not aliased
with a factor. Retained samples will be stored for each run under the site retention policy.

## Statistical methods {#sec-stats}

All analysis will be performed on coded factors. Each factor is coded so that its set-point
is zero and the edges of its characterization range are minus one and plus one, which makes
the estimated effects directly comparable across parameters measured in different units
(pH units, degrees Celsius, mmHg, mOsm and days). The analysis will be performed under
SOP-1002.

The screening data will be fitted by ordinary least squares to a model containing the
`{python} k_scr` main effects and the `{python} n_2fi` two-factor interactions. An effect is
reported as twice the coded coefficient, which is the change in the response across the full
range of the factor. Significance is judged at α = 0.05. That model estimates
`{python} n_scr_terms` terms from `{python} n_scr` runs and leaves `{python} df_scr` residual
degrees of freedom, so it is close to saturated. A near-saturated model identifies which
factors are active, and it is not used to predict. The division is deliberate and is carried
through the whole analysis. The screening design identifies the effects, and the
response-surface model is the predictive model and the basis of the design space.

The response-surface data will be fitted to a full quadratic model in the `{python} k_rsm`
factors carried forward, containing the main effects, the two-factor interactions and the
`{python} n_rsm_quad` pure quadratic terms. That model estimates `{python} n_rsm_terms` terms
from `{python} n_rsm` runs and leaves `{python} df_rsm` residual degrees of freedom, which is
enough to support prediction and to test the fit. Model adequacy will be assessed on the
overall F test, on R², on adjusted R², and on predicted R² computed from the PRESS statistic.
It will also be assessed by an ANOVA partition of the residual into lack of fit and pure
error, using the centre-point replicates described in @sec-sampling. A model whose lack of
fit is significant against pure error will not be used to define the design space.

A parameter with no active term in either model is not discarded. It is reported as a null
result, classified on that basis under SOP-4001, and retained in the knowledge space as
evidence that the attribute is robust to it over the range screened. A parameter that is
inactive across the whole characterization range supports a stronger robustness statement
than one shown to be inactive across its normal operating range alone.

Commercial-scale capability will be estimated by Monte-Carlo simulation of `{python} N_MC`
batches at the normal operating condition. Each of the `{python} k_rsm` factors of the
response-surface model is drawn from a normal distribution centred on its set-point, with a
standard deviation of one sixth of the width of its normal operating range, and every draw is
constrained to the characterization range. The fitted model then predicts each response for
every simulated batch. The parameters the model does not contain are held at their set-points
in the simulation, and their contribution is bounded separately by the univariate assessment
(@sec-univariate).

Capability will be reported as a Cpk for each response, with the margin between the predicted
mean and the limit that binds. Afucosylation, galactosylation and high mannose are judged
against two-sided acceptance criteria, so their Cpk is the smaller of the two one-sided
indices, the one against the lower limit and the one against the upper limit. Acidic variants
and aggregates are judged against an upper limit only (@sec-par), so their Cpk is the
one-sided index against that limit. The two proven acceptable range analyses are described
separately in @sec-par, because they answer a different question from capability.

# Study design {#sec-design}

The design answers two questions in sequence. A screening study resolves which of the
`{python} k_scr` multivariate parameters are active on which response, and a
response-surface study over the active subset produces the predictive model. The univariate
work (@sec-univariate) runs alongside and bounds the parameters that the risk assessment did
not send to the factorial design.

## Factors, ranges and study type {#sec-factors}

@tbl-params gives the set-point, the normal operating range and the characterization range
of every parameter of this step, with the study type assigned in RA-001.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(_pp)
print()
print(": Production bioreactor parameters, ranges and study type. The range studied is the "
      "characterization range and is not a proven acceptable range. {#tbl-params}")
```

The two ranges in the table do different jobs, and PCR-003 will keep them apart. The normal
operating range is where the commercial process will be held, and it sets the dispersion of
the capability simulation (@sec-stats). The range studied is the knowledge space edge, and it
is the range over which the fitted models are valid. The design space lies between the two.
It is the part of the characterized space in which every attribute is predicted to meet its
criterion (@sec-acceptance), and the normal operating range of every parameter has to sit
inside it.

Culture pH is held to `{python} nor_of('pH', False)` in routine operation and will be studied
over `{python} rng_of('pH', False)`. Culture temperature is held to
`{python} nor_of('temperature')` and studied over `{python} rng_of('temperature')`.
Dissolved carbon dioxide moves from a normal range of `{python} nor_of('co2')` to a studied
range of `{python} rng_of('co2')`, because pCO~2~ accumulates with scale and is not held by a
control loop at commercial scale (it follows vessel height, sparge rate and cell density), so
its excursions have to be bounded by data. Culture duration will be studied over
`{python} rng_of('duration')` around a set-point of `{python} sp_of('duration')`, which
brackets both an early and a late harvest decision.

@tbl-legend gives the letter code used for each factor in the design matrices and in the
effect tables of PCR-003. The letters follow the screening order and are reused unchanged for
the response-surface terms, so that a term such as AB means the same pair of factors in both
analyses. Its last column states the anticipated response-surface subset described in
@sec-rsm, and that subset is subject to the screening result.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(D.factor_legend_df(UO))
print()
print(": Factor legend for the coded design matrices. {#tbl-legend}")
```

## Screening design {#sec-screening}

The screening study is a two-level fractional factorial in the `{python} k_scr` multivariate
factors, augmented with `{python} n_scr_c` centre points, for `{python} n_scr` runs in total.
The `{python} n_scr_fact` factorial runs are a half fraction of the `{python} n_full` run
full factorial, chosen at resolution V so that every main effect and every two-factor
interaction is estimable clear of the others. Two-factor interactions are aliased with
three-factor interactions, which the platform history gives no reason to expect at this step
(see @sec-risks for how that assumption is managed). The planned matrix is given in
@tbl-appa.

The purpose of the screening study is to identify the parameters that have the largest
effect on each quality attribute, and to identify which pairs of parameters interact. It is
not intended to describe curvature and it will not be used to predict. Runs will be executed
in a randomized order, and where an operational constraint requires the runs to be split into
blocks, the block will be recorded and tested as a term in the model.

## Response-surface design {#sec-rsm}

The response-surface study is a face-centred central composite design in the subset of
factors that screening identifies as active. It comprises `{python} n_rsm_fact` factorial
runs, `{python} n_rsm_ax` axial runs at the faces of the cube and `{python} n_rsm_c` centre
points, for `{python} n_rsm` runs in total. Placing the axial points on the faces keeps every
run inside the characterization range. A rotatable design would put its axial runs outside
the ranges given in @tbl-params, and the fitted model is declared only over the ranges
characterized. The planned matrix is given in @tbl-appb.

The design has been sized for `{python} k_rsm` factors. Prior knowledge indicates that
culture pH, culture temperature, culture duration and dissolved carbon dioxide are the
factors most likely to be carried forward, and @tbl-appb is drawn for that subset. If the
screening analysis identifies a different set of active factors, the design will be
re-specified on the same principles before execution, and the change will be recorded against
this plan.

This design adds the pure quadratic terms and therefore resolves curvature within the
characterized ranges. It is the model that will be used to predict mean response levels, to
draw the response surfaces, to derive the proven acceptable ranges (@sec-par) and to define
the design space reported in PCR-003.

## Univariate assessment {#sec-univariate}

Dissolved oxygen, initial viable cell concentration, basal medium concentration and nutrient
feed-1 volume will each be assessed one at a time. Each parameter will be run at the low and
high edges of its characterization range with every other parameter at its set-point, and the
results will be compared against the centre-point condition of the multivariate design. The
same analytical panel applies, so a univariate result is directly comparable with a factorial
result on the same response.

These `{python} n_par_uni` parameters were not placed in the factorial design because the
risk assessment scored them below the multivariate threshold, and the reasons are
mechanistic. Dissolved
oxygen is held to `{python} nor_of('do')` by a control loop with ample authority, and it acts
on the culture through growth and not through the glycan chemistry. Initial viable cell
concentration is set at inoculation, and its effect on the culture is largely absorbed within
the first days of a culture lasting `{python} sp_of('duration')`. Basal medium concentration
and nutrient feed-1 volume are delivered by weight against a recipe, and prior platform work
has bounded their effect on the glycan profile as shallow [@amab2009]. A univariate range
statement is the appropriate level of evidence for a parameter of that kind, and PCR-003 will
report it as such rather than implying that it carries the weight of a multivariate result.

# Acceptance and decision criteria {#sec-acceptance}

This section states the decisions that will be taken on the data before the data exist. Every
criterion below has to be met for the study to support the design space and the parameter
classifications that PCR-003 will report.

The scale-down model is qualified when the bench-scale runs at the target condition are shown
to be equivalent to the at-scale data for the growth and productivity profile and for the
`{python} n_resp` quality responses. Equivalence is assessed against a pre-defined acceptance
margin on each compared attribute, and the margins are defined in the qualification protocol
issued under SOP-1001 (@sec-sdm). Characterization runs executed before that qualification is
approved will not be used to define the design space.

A fitted model is adequate when the overall F test is significant at α = 0.05, when the lack
of fit is not significant against pure error, and when adjusted R² and predicted R² are
consistent with each other. A large gap between adjusted and predicted R² indicates a model
that fits the runs it was fitted to and predicts new conditions poorly, and such a model will
be reduced to its significant terms before it is used. A model that fails on lack of fit will
be reported with its diagnostics and will not be used to define the design space.

The design space will be declared over that part of the characterized space in which the
fitted response-surface model predicts every attribute in @tbl-cqa to lie within its
acceptance criterion. The region will be reported in the planes of the factor pairs that carry
the largest interactions, and the worst-case corner of the region, which is the combination of
settings that comes closest to a limit, will be identified and stated. The normal operating
range must lie inside the declared region for every parameter. If it does not, the finding
will be reported as an edge of failure, and the normal operating range will be narrowed
instead of the region being widened.

Capability will be reported as a Cpk per attribute with the margin to the binding limit,
computed as described in @sec-stats. This plan sets no numerical minimum for Cpk. The
acceptance framework for capability is given in PCMP-001 and applies across the campaign.

A parameter will be classified under SOP-4001 from two inputs, the demonstrated effect of the
parameter on a quality attribute and the capability of the commercial equipment to hold it
inside the design space [@amab2009]. A parameter with a demonstrated effect on a critical
attribute and a high risk of falling outside the design space is a critical process parameter
(CPP). One with a demonstrated effect but a low risk of falling outside the design space is a
well-controlled critical process parameter (WC-CPP). A parameter that affects process
performance without affecting a quality attribute is a key process parameter (KPP), and one
with no demonstrated effect on either is a general process parameter (GPP). The classification
itself is an outcome, and it is reported in PCR-003.

An excursion from this plan during execution will be recorded as a deviation, investigated and
impact assessed before the affected data are used. A run whose executed condition still falls
inside the characterized ranges may be retained with a documented justification and analysed
at its executed setting, because the fitted model is estimated from the conditions actually
run. A run whose condition falls outside those ranges, or whose input material is not
representative of the process, invalidates the affected design for the purpose of defining the
design space, and that design will be re-executed in full. Both dispositions, and the
reasoning behind whichever is applied, will be reported in the deviations section of PCR-003.

The study passes when the scale-down model is qualified, the models are adequate, the design
space contains the normal operating range for every parameter, every attribute meets its
acceptance criterion across that region, and every parameter carries a documented
classification. The conclusions will be bounded to the ranges characterized, to the fitted
models and to the qualified scale-down model, and they will not be extended to conditions
outside the studied space.

# Proven acceptable ranges (planned analysis) {#sec-par}

The design space is a multivariate region, and a reader also needs the range of each parameter
taken on its own. PCR-003 will therefore report a proven acceptable range for every
combination of a governed attribute and a response-surface parameter, derived from the fitted
model by the analysis described here.

The acceptance basis is the drug substance criterion recorded for each attribute in the
quality attribute register (@tbl-cqa). Afucosylation, galactosylation and high mannose are
judged against two-sided criteria, and acidic variants and aggregates against an upper limit
only. The risk to the product from both of those attributes is an elevated level. The lower
edge recorded for acidic variants in @tbl-cqa is the range of experience from the clinical
campaigns and not a binding specification, so both the decision rule below and the capability
index described in @sec-stats are judged against the upper bound alone. No viral clearance
response arises at this step, so no step-level requirement has to be back-calculated from a
cumulative requirement, and that case belongs to the viral steps (PCP-006, PCP-008 and
PCP-009).

Two analyses will be run for each pair. The first analysis holds the other parameters at their
set-points and evaluates the fitted response-surface model across the characterization range
of the parameter of interest. The second analysis propagates the normal operating ranges of
the other parameters by Monte-Carlo, drawing each of them inside its normal operating range
and adding the model residual variation, on a grid of `{python} D.PAR_GRID` points across the
characterization range with `{python} N_PAR_MC` draws at each grid point. The random draw uses
a fixed seed, so the reported ranges are reproducible from the same data.

The decision rule is the same in both analyses. The proven acceptable range is the contiguous
interval of the parameter, containing the set-point, over which the attribute stays within its
acceptance criterion. In the first analysis that means the predicted mean stays within the
criterion, and in the second it means the ninety-five per cent predictive interval stays
within the criterion, which is a robustness statement and is expected to give the narrower of
the two ranges. Where the set-point condition itself fails the criterion, no proven acceptable
range exists for that pair, and PCR-003 will report it as such.

Each governed attribute will be reported with a two-panel plot for its governing parameter,
which is the parameter carrying the largest main effect on that attribute. The parameter is on
the horizontal axis and the attribute on the vertical axis, the acceptance limit is drawn, the
acceptable region is shaded green, and the set-point and the normal operating range are
marked. The left panel shows the first analysis and the right panel shows the Monte-Carlo
analysis with its predictive interval.

The relationship between these ranges and the design space will be stated explicitly in
PCR-003. A proven acceptable range is a univariate statement about one parameter, and the
second analysis extends it to co-variation of the others within their normal ranges. The design
space is the multivariate region, and it is not the product of the individual proven acceptable
ranges. Where a parameter's whole characterization range is proven acceptable under both
analyses, the binding constraint is the worst-case corner of the design space and not that
parameter's univariate range, and PCR-003 will say which constraint binds. Every range
reported will be bounded to the characterization ranges in @tbl-params and to the fitted
model.

# Data management and integrity {#sec-data}

All study records will meet ALCOA+ expectations. Run set-points, control system trends and
in-process measurements are captured in the bioreactor control system and its historian, and
are transferred to the electronic laboratory notebook against the run identifier. Analytical
raw data are captured in the chromatography data system and in the plate reader software for
the immunoassays, with audit trails enabled and access controlled by role.

The design matrices, the executed conditions and the assembled response data set will be held
as a version-controlled data set, and the statistical analysis will be executed from a
version-controlled script under SOP-1002. That is what makes the reported effects, models and
ranges reproducible from the raw data by a reviewer who was not present at the bench. Any
change to the data set after analysis requires a documented reason, a re-run of the analysis
and a second-person review.

Every record is reviewed by a second person before it is used in the report. Deviations,
including any executed condition that departs from the design, are recorded in the quality
system as they are detected and not retrospectively. Records are retained under the site
retention policy.

# Roles and responsibilities {#sec-roles}

The functions listed in @tbl-roles carry the study, and the approval record at the front of
this document (@tbl-appr) binds the same functions to the plan.

| Function | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| Process Development / MSAT | Owns the plan, executes the scale-down runs, performs the analysis and writes PCR-003 |
| Analytical Development | Maintains the validated methods, analyses the samples and reports assay performance |
| Manufacturing Science (receiving site) | Reviews the ranges and the control assumptions for feasibility at commercial scale |
| Statistics | Reviews the designs before execution and the fitted models before reporting |
| Quality Assurance | Approves this plan and PCR-003, and oversees deviation handling |

: Functions and responsibilities for the study. {#tbl-roles}

The statistical review before execution is the last point at which the factor set, the ranges
and the run count can still be changed. The review by manufacturing science at the receiving
site checks the characterized ranges against what the commercial vessel can hold.

# Deliverables and schedule {#sec-schedule}

The deliverable of this plan is PCR-003, the process characterization report for the
production bioreactor. It will contain the executed designs, the effect and coefficient
tables, the model diagnostics, the design space, the proven acceptable ranges, the capability
estimate, the classification of every parameter and any deviations recorded during execution.
PCR-003 rolls up into the master report (PCMR-001) together with the reports of the other
steps.

The work runs in five phases, and the order is fixed by dependency and not by convenience.
Scale-down model qualification comes first and is approved before any characterization run.
The screening campaign follows, and its analysis fixes the factor subset for the
response-surface campaign (@sec-rsm). The response-surface campaign and the univariate runs
follow, and they may be interleaved as scale-down system capacity allows, because the
univariate runs do not depend on the screening result. The capability and proven acceptable
range analyses are performed on the fitted models once the response-surface data are
complete, and the report is written last.

No calendar dates are committed in this plan. The schedule is held in the campaign plan
(PCMP-001), and it depends on scale-down system availability and on the analytical throughput
for the methods listed in @tbl-amv.

# Risks and assumptions {#sec-risks}

The study rests on assumptions that would change its conclusions if they proved false, and
they are stated here so that PCR-003 can report against them.

The principal risk is that the scale-down model does not represent the commercial vessel over
the whole characterized space. Qualification demonstrates equivalence at the target condition,
and it does not demonstrate equivalence at the edges of the ranges, where mixing and gas
transfer differ most between scales. This is managed in three ways, by matching the
scale-dependent parameters on performance and not on geometry (@sec-sdm), by reporting the
pCO~2~ and osmolality trajectories for every run, and by confirming the design space at
commercial scale during Stage 2. The design space reported in PCR-003 will not be confirmed at
scale at the edges of the ranges.

The second risk is analytical. The glycan responses come from a single separation
(@sec-analytics), so an assay shift moves `{python} n_glyc` of the `{python} n_resp` responses
together and can imitate a process effect. The centre-point replicates and the randomized run
order are the controls for this, and any effect of the same size as the assay reproducibility
will be reported as such.

The third risk is material. A change of basal medium or feed lot during the campaign
introduces a variable that the design does not carry, and the effect of such a change on the
glycan profile is not negligible. Lot usage will be recorded per run, so that a lot change can
be tested as a term if the data suggest it.

Three assumptions are made explicit. Platform behaviour observed on the earlier products
(X-Mab, Y-Mab and Z-Mab) is assumed to transfer to A-Mab, which is the basis for studying
`{python} n_par_mv` parameters instead of the full list. The parameter list in @tbl-params is
assumed to be complete, which rests on the process description in PTP-001 and on the risk
assessment. Three-factor interactions are assumed to be negligible, which is what allows the
resolution V fraction described in @sec-screening. That assumption is carried on platform
history, and the `{python} df_scr` residual degrees of freedom the screening model leaves are
too few to test it. The control is the response-surface campaign, where a two-factor
interaction that the screening analysis estimated and the response-surface model does not
reproduce will be reported as evidence that the assumption was broken. A pair involving a
factor that is not carried forward, such as osmolality under the subset anticipated in
@sec-rsm, cannot be checked in that way.

# Approvals {#sec-approvals}

This plan is effective when it has been approved by every function in the approval record at
the front of the document (@tbl-appr). Execution may not begin before that approval. Any
change to the design, to the ranges or to the acceptance criteria after approval requires a
revision of this plan under the site change control procedure.
